preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 10000 for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit() and len(line.split()) == 1) and all(0 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 10000 and 0 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 10000 and 1 <= int(line.split()[2]) <= 99 for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit() and len(line.split()) == 3) and all(0 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 10000 and 0 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 10000 for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit() and len(line.split()) == 2)
preconditions.description: The first line contains two integers V (1 ≤ V ≤ 10000) and E (0 ≤ E ≤ 200000). Each of the next E lines contains three integers u, v, w (0 ≤ u, v ≤ V-1, 1 ≤ w ≤ 99) representing a directed edge u → v with weight w. The last line contains two integers s, t (0 ≤ s, t ≤ V-1). The graph has no self-loops or multiple directed edges between the same pair of vertices.
The input has exactly E + 2 lines: one for V and E, E lines for edges, and one for s and t.

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer representing the number of different shortest paths from s to t, where two paths are different if they contain at least one distinct edge. The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= u <= V-1 and 0 <= v <= V-1 and 1 <= w <= 99 for u, v, w in [(int(line.split()[0]), int(line.split()[1]), int(line.split()[2])) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:E+1]])
postconditions.description: The edges in the graph are valid: each edge u → v has weight w where u, v are vertices and w is a positive integer ≤ 99.

postconditions.expression: s == t == int(stdout.strip()) if s == t else (int(stdout.strip()) == 0 if not any(u == s and v == t for u, v, _ in [(int(line.split()[0]), int(line.split()[1]), int(line.split()[2])) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:E+1]]) else int(stdout.strip()) >= 1)
postconditions.description: If s equals t, the output is 1 (only the trivial path). If s and t are disconnected, the output is 0. Otherwise, the output is the count of distinct shortest paths from s to t.
